headline: President Trump extends again the delay in enforcing a federal law against the TikTok app.
what_it_does: This order pushes back, once more, the date when the federal government will start enforcing rules against TikTok. A 2024 federal law requires TikTok to be sold by its China-based owner or be blocked in the US, and earlier orders had already delayed enforcement. No summary was provided, so the new deadline and other details are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: People in the US who use TikTok
who_it_affects.how: They can likely keep using the app while enforcement stays on hold.
The company gets more time before the government acts against it under the law.

who_it_affects.group: App stores and internet hosting companies
who_it_affects.how: They face a delay before any penalties for offering or supporting TikTok would be enforced.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed September 16, 2025; the length of the new delay is not stated in the source provided.
